title: Statistical Thermodynamics
tagline: The Boltzmann distribution, partition functions, thermodynamic functions, ensembles, equilibrium constants, real gases, quantum statistics and rate theory
summary: Statistical thermodynamics connects the energy levels of molecules with the bulk properties measured in the laboratory. This course derives the Boltzmann distribution and the partition function, computes thermodynamic functions and equilibrium constants from molecular data, and extends the theory to interacting molecules, quantum statistics and the rates of reactions.

chapters.title: The Boltzmann distribution
chapters.summary: Configurations and weights, the most probable distribution, and the meaning of temperature.

chapters.title: The molecular partition function
chapters.summary: Translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic partition functions and how to evaluate them.

chapters.title: Thermodynamic functions from partition functions
chapters.summary: Internal energy, heat capacity and entropy from the partition function, and the equipartition theorem.

chapters.title: The canonical ensemble
chapters.summary: Ensembles, the canonical partition function, fluctuations, and independent and indistinguishable molecules.

chapters.title: Equilibrium constants from molecular data
chapters.summary: Equilibrium constants in terms of partition functions, with applications to dissociation and isotope exchange.

chapters.title: Interacting molecules: real gases and liquids
chapters.summary: The configuration integral, virial coefficients and intermolecular potentials, and the radial distribution function of liquids.

chapters.title: Quantum statistics
chapters.summary: Bose–Einstein and Fermi–Dirac statistics, electrons in metals, and the Einstein and Debye models of the heat capacity of solids.

chapters.title: Statistical theories of reaction rates
chapters.summary: Transition-state theory from partition functions, and the Lindemann and RRKM theories of unimolecular reactions.
